xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4223: Official gauntlet loop support: pan lane (launch/list/wait/report/reap), lanes nested under their orchestrator, any-harness orchestrators

plan.title: Official gauntlet loop support: pan lane (launch/list/wait/report/reap), lanes nested under their orchestrator, any-harness orchestrators
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: The operator filed and decided this as one feature (PRD Q1-Q3: verb, reap-archives, successor nesting), and the parts interlock: the lane door, the parent-link schema, the fork stamp and the two nesting views share one data contract (parent_conversation_id plus three lane columns). The documentation work item alone spans more than 6 lint subsystems (reference/, configuration/, docs/, sync-sources/, CLAUDE.md, docs.json), so no split into sibling issues passes the projected-surface gate cleanly. The plan compensates with 24 small items, an explicit DAG, and two deep-inspected foundation items.

narratives.Problem: Gauntlet orchestrators fan out lanes by hand. Claude orchestrators use the Agent tool (Anthropic models only); other models abuse `pan handoff` from a throwaway conversation because handoff ignores --harness. The result is about a dozen flat 'SB lane: …' conversations parented (inside fork_request JSON) to the wrong row, a hand-rolled sentinel.log completion signal, duplicate lanes sharing a worktree, runaway lanes nobody sees, and manual teardown. GPT, Codex and Kimi orchestrators cannot fan out at all.
narratives.Proposal: Follow .pan/drafts/pan-4223.md. A lane is an ordinary conversation carrying four write-once launch-time columns (parent_conversation_id, gauntlet_run, lane_key, lane_role); lane status is derived on read. One core (launchLane) behind POST /api/lanes and `pan lane start` creates the per-lane worktree under a configurable lanes root, writes the brief, and starts a conversation with any harness/model/effort through the extracted startConversationRuntime. `pan lane list|wait|report|stop|reap` reuse the worker report and wait machinery, the conversation stop door and the archive door (reap archives by default, --keep retains). handleConversationSummaryFork stamps the parent link so handoff/fork successors nest. The Command Deck and the Agents page nest rows by parent link, capped at display depth 2. pan tell resolves a conversation's real harness and refuses to re-task a critic that reported. The pan-gauntlet-loop skill adopts the lane door and the GAUNTLET-LOOP-V3 rules.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Serving the gauntlet progress page from the dashboard; the skill's http.server page stays.
- Modeling verdicts, board statuses, merges or releases in Overdeck; they stay in the project repo.
- Machine-level rig limits (browser slots, ports, displays); they stay in the project's run file.
- Changing pan handoff, pan fork or pan worker behavior beyond the parent link on fork successors and cross-reference docs; a handoff of a lane does not carry lane facts to its successor.
- A per-run Herdr workspace or a parent pane token.
- Automatic lane launching or scheduling; the orchestrator decides every launch.
- Re-parenting or backfilling existing rows (including HOTEL conversations 2899-2910).
- Parent links on post-/clear siblings, backfilled agent rows, retrospective conversations or POST /api/conversations rows.
- A stored lane status field or a run table.
- Accepting effort xhigh at the lane door.
- Killing any process during reap, or `git worktree remove --force`.
- A `pan lane tell` verb (messaging stays `pan tell`).

autoDecisions.summary: Keep PAN-4223 as one issue and set plan.metadata.sizeJustification instead of filing sibling issues.
autoDecisions.rationale: The operator filed and decided the design as one unit; the docs item alone exceeds the 6-subsystem lint limit, so a split cannot pass the gate cleanly; 24 small items with explicit edges keep review granular.

autoDecisions.summary: Split PRD work items WI-3, WI-5, WI-6, WI-10, WI-11 and WI-13 into smaller xBRIEF items; move the reap route from WI-5 into the reap item.
autoDecisions.rationale: The planning rules require the smallest defensible items; the reap route imports reapLane, so it belongs with WI-7.

autoDecisions.summary: Run frontend tests through `npm --prefix ./src/dashboard/frontend run test -- <paths>` and corrected AC-10/AC-11 in the PRD.
autoDecisions.rationale: The root vitest.config.ts excludes src/dashboard/frontend/**, so the PRD's root `npx vitest run` commands for frontend files would run nothing.

autoDecisions.summary: Only lane-columns (conversations.ts, at its 1111 cap) and runtime-start-extract (conversation-runtime.ts, at its 1186 cap) own scripts/file-size-allowlist.txt, ordered by an edge; cli/index.ts (cap 1379) and projects.ts (cap 1210) have headroom and the reap change adds no lines to routes/conversations.ts.
autoDecisions.rationale: scripts/lint-file-size.sh fails a file only above its allowlisted cap; limiting the shared allowlist to the two capped files avoids needless serialization.

autoDecisions.summary: The lane door passes `undefined` as the explicit harness when neither --harness nor gauntlet.roles config names one.
autoDecisions.rationale: concerns.md records that coalescing to 'claude-code' bypasses the provider default in resolveHarness; the PRD's any-harness goal depends on the provider default applying.

autoDecisions.summary: The AC-10 live Command Deck screenshot is a test/UAT-role check, not a work-item gate; work items do not run `pan reload`.
autoDecisions.rationale: The PRD already names the component tests as the gate with the screenshot as a fallback-at-next-reload; only the flywheel deploys.

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/lanes/wait.ts per .pan/drafts/pan-4223.md WI-6 step 4. waitForLane(name, opts, deps) calls waitForWorkerReport('conv-' + name, …) with isAlive from conversationHarnessAlive, idleAgeMs from the lane view (activity 'working' → 0, else now - lastActivityAt, null when unknown), fetchLastAssistantMessage from GET /api/conversations/:name/messages (see the PRD implementation checkpoint and its null fallback), and resolveTranscriptPath from the conversation's session file. waitForLaneSet({ run | parent }, { after, timeoutMs }) polls every 2 s and returns the first report whose cursor '<atMs>.<name>.<seq>' sorts after `after`, oldest first (ties by name then seq); on timeout it returns the timeout outcome with the next cursor; each poll prints one stderr warning per lane that is stopped with no report since the cursor.
